ai_security_governance_definition.description: AISGD (AI Security Governance Definition) is an additive domain governance definition for governing security risks that arise when AI systems, AI use, AI agents, AI-mediated inputs and outputs, tools, retrieval, memory, authorization interpretation, or information flows become attack surfaces, leakage paths, policy-bypass paths, or privilege-misuse paths. AISGD governs AI-specific security risk, including prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, instruction leakage, AI-mediated secret or private-data exposure, tool abuse, agentic workflow takeover, retrieval poisoning, memory contamination, authorization confusion, policy bypass, and cross-agent attack. AISGD does not absorb general cybersecurity, does not implement secure engineering by itself, does not define model policy by itself, does not govern ordinary agentic execution by itself, does not finalize decision authority, does not audit strategic decisions, and does not expand blocking conditions beyond the declared AI-security basis.

sibling_domain_boundary.purpose: Keep AISGD limited to AI-security risk governance while preserving handoff readiness to adjacent domains without absorbing them.

aagd.name: Agentic AI Governance Definition
aagd.aisgd_boundary: AISGD may flag agentic takeover, unsafe tool authority, or cross-agent attack risk, but must not govern ordinary agentic execution, side-effect scheduling, or tool workflow management itself.

airgd.name: AI Research Governance Definition
airgd.aisgd_boundary: AISGD may flag security exposure in research AI systems or research tooling, but must not substitute AI research design, validation, or investigation governance.

mpgd.name: Model Policy Governance Definition
mpgd.aisgd_boundary: AISGD may flag model-mediated security boundary failures or policy bypass risks, but must not create or finalize model-use policy as a whole.

segd.name: Software Engineering Governance Definition
segd.aisgd_boundary: AISGD may define AI-security repair requirements, but implementation, architecture realization, and system change remain outside AISGD.

dsgd.name: Data Science Governance Definition
dsgd.aisgd_boundary: AISGD may govern AI-mediated data leakage, poisoning, or exfiltration risk, but must not substitute statistical, modeling, or data-analysis validity governance.

acrgd.name: Artifact Composition and Review Governance Definition
acrgd.aisgd_boundary: AISGD may flag AI-mediated leakage or attack-surface risk in an artifact process, but must not absorb artifact composition, publication readiness, or general disclosure review.

omrgd.name: Operations, Maintenance, and Reliability Governance Definition
omrgd.aisgd_boundary: AISGD may flag AI-security incident risk or recurrence requirements, but must not absorb ordinary operations, monitoring, restoration, or reliability governance.

daagd.name: Decision Authority and Accountability Governance Definition
daagd.aisgd_boundary: AISGD may flag AI-mediated authorization confusion or privilege misuse risk, but must not finalize who may decide, who is accountable, or whether approval is required.

sppgd.name: Strategic Planning and Prioritization Governance Definition
sppgd.aisgd_boundary: AISGD may flag security risk that affects strategic structure, but must not generate strategic planning, prioritization, selection, non-selection, retreat, or continuation judgment.

sdagd.name: Strategic Decision Audit Governance Definition
sdagd.aisgd_boundary: AISGD may provide AI-security findings for audit context, but must not audit strategic decisions as passed, conditionally passed, returned, or invalidated.

sdmrgd.name: Strategic Decision Meta-Review Governance Definition
sdmrgd.aisgd_boundary: AISGD must not meta-review SDAGD; AI-security observations may be input material only when relevant.

domain_scope.scope_statement: Govern security risks that arise when AI systems, AI use, AI agents, AI-mediated inputs and outputs, tools, retrieval, memory, authorization interpretation, or information flows become attack surfaces, leakage paths, policy-bypass paths, or privilege-misuse paths.

role_complete_separation.principle: AISGD must keep AI-security risk governance, source material, untrusted context, inherited governance, sibling domain references, governed targets, evaluation, repair, activation, status reporting, records, external orchestration, and metadata responsibilities separated.

separation_targets.source_material: inputs, external documents, retrieval content, memory content, tool results, logs, or prior materials used for AI-security assessment; source content is not trusted or absorbed by default
separation_targets.untrusted_context: external or retrieved material treated as data or reference unless authorized as instruction by higher authority
separation_targets.ai_security_risk_governance: AISGD-owned detection and governance of AI-mediated attack surface, leakage, privilege misuse, policy bypass, and malicious-context risk
separation_targets.ordinary_security_reference: ordinary security concepts referenced only to the extent required by AI-mediated risk and not absorbed as general cybersecurity governance
separation_targets.inherited_governance: parent ARGD and DAGD governance referenced as authoritative context and not re-expanded inside AISGD
separation_targets.sibling_reference: other domain definitions referenced only when in scope and not absorbed into AISGD
separation_targets.governed_target: the AI-mediated input, context, tool, memory, output, authority interpretation, information flow, or workflow being governed
separation_targets.domain_evaluation: AISGD-specific checks for prompt injection, leakage, tool abuse, agentic takeover, retrieval or memory contamination, authorization confusion, and boundary preservation
separation_targets.domain_repair: AISGD-specific repair origins and revalidation scopes, not implementation, policy, operations, artifact, authority, or strategic repair itself
separation_targets.activation: local AI-security applicability signals only; routing and priority remain external
separation_targets.status_reporting: AISGD delta reporting only, not broad runtime status replacement
separation_targets.records: AISGD records that remain structurally separate from evaluation, repair, and metadata
separation_targets.external_orchestration: CDOGD routing, registry, priority, activation, and function assignment remain external to AISGD
separation_targets.metadata: identity, authorship, license, repository, and compatibility information remain metadata, not AI-security rules

abstraction_and_context_policy.purpose: Keep AISGD applicable to AI-security risk across AI systems, AI use, AI agents, tools, retrieval, memory, and AI-mediated outputs without reducing it to a specific platform, tool, workflow, organization, or attack example.

ai_security_risk_model.purpose: Classify AI-mediated security risks without converting examples into exhaustive or universal rules.

risk_categories.prompt_injection: External input or embedded document content attempts to override higher-priority instructions or manipulate AI behavior.
risk_categories.jailbreak: Input attempts to bypass runtime, policy, or safety boundaries and elicit prohibited, unsafe, or boundary-breaking output or action.
risk_categories.instruction_leakage: System, developer, internal policy, hidden instruction, or other non-public instruction boundary may be exposed.
risk_categories.tool_abuse: AI tool use may cause unauthorized, excessive, deceptive, or side-effectful operation or information access.
risk_categories.agentic_takeover: An agentic workflow may be controlled or redirected by malicious input, external context, compromised handoff, or unsafe tool result.
risk_categories.data_exfiltration: AI may expose secrets, credentials, private data, internal information, or authority-restricted information through output, tool use, memory, retrieval, or handoff.
risk_categories.retrieval_poisoning: RAG, retrieval, search, or external context may contain malicious or misleading content that contaminates AI reasoning or output.
risk_categories.memory_contamination: Persistent or continuing context may contain inappropriate, malicious, stale, or unauthorized content that affects future behavior.
risk_categories.authorization_confusion: AI may misidentify requester authority, approval status, delegated scope, or who may request or execute an action.
risk_categories.policy_bypass: AI-mediated workflow may bypass required constraints, review, approval, confirmation, or runtime boundaries.
risk_categories.cross_agent_attack: Multiple agents or handoffs may be used to bypass constraints, hide malicious context, or create privilege or instruction boundary confusion.

repair.purpose: Repair AISGD failures by identifying AI-security repair origins, restoring affected security boundaries, selecting bounded repair directions, and handing off implementation, policy, operations, authority, artifact, strategy, or agentic execution work to the responsible domain when outside AISGD.

ai_security_scope_self_doubt_check.purpose: Confirm that AISGD is in a valid AI-security posture and is not overstepping into general cybersecurity, implementation, model policy, ordinary agentic execution, artifact review, decision authority, strategic planning, or strategic audit.

ai_security_assessment_record.purpose: Record AI-security assessment for AI input, external context, retrieval, memory, tool use, agentic workflow, authorization context, output security, detected risks, blocking conditions, repair, and handoff.

ai_security_repair_and_handoff_record.schema_name: AISGD AI Security Repair and Handoff Record
ai_security_repair_and_handoff_record.purpose: Record AISGD repair origin, affected boundary, repair direction, handoff target, revalidation requirement, residual risk, and ready-claim status after repair.

ai_security_scope_self_doubt_record.schema_name: AISGD AI Security Scope Self-Doubt Record
ai_security_scope_self_doubt_record.purpose: Record AISGD's lightweight self-doubt check for overreach, overblocking, underblocking, and handoff correctness without treating the check as external audit, self-approval, or final authority.

record_relationship_contract.purpose: Define relationships among AI-security assessment, repair and handoff, and scope self-doubt records without implementing sibling-domain records.
